messages.subject: Prohibitively slow sdreport() with many random effects
messages.subject_clean: Prohibitively slow sdreport() with many random effects
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am having trouble with the sdreport() function in a model with many (tens of thousands) of random effects. I think this may be a more generalized issue, but allow me to use my specific situation as an example.

I am trying to fit an SPDE model over a rather large geographical area, and with a time dimension as well. This results in many many random effects, exponentially increasing with an increasingly finer geographical mesh. Fit times using nlminb() are good - a bit faster than INLA's empirical-bayes setting in fact. The problem comes in when trying to get the variance-covariance matrix out of sdreport(), where it grinds to a halt.

I think I have located the bottleneck within sdreport(), its an lapply() within the sdreport::doDeltaMethod() sub-function. This is essentially looping the sdreport::doDeltaMethod::reverse.sweep() function over all random effects in the model. (see line 228 here: https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/master/TMB/R/sdreport.R)
A <- t(do.call("cbind",lapply(seq_along(phi), reverse.sweep))) + Dphi.fixed
Now, I thought to just do the quick thing and try making it an mclapply(), but within reverse.sweep(), the obj$env$f function is called, and has superassignment (<<-) operators. Now, I think this makes multithreading an issue because these environmental changes are not passed around, and thus mclapply() simply doesnt work.

And thus I am stuck with a big model that takes a prohibitively long time in sdreport(). Are we stuck with this issue on models with a large number of random effects? Hopefully I am missing something easy here? I am wondering if anyone has faced, an overcome, this issue, or has suggestions.

Thanks,
Roy

messages.body_plain:
It's hard to give further advice without a specific reproducible example. At this point I'm guessing you are seeking the standard errors of all random effects in the model? Those are already in the output from sdreport. Use summary(sdr,"random").

PS: You should definitely never attempt to invert the joint precision of a large space-time model. There's always an alternative...
